content:
Turns out I need to make use of yet another niche area of mathematics for the CGT repo. The precise result I need is Lemma 3.4 from Lenstra (1977), which can be stated as follows:

Let Q be the quadratic closure of 𝔽₂, and let x be algebraic over Q. The group of units Q(x)ˣ is generated by x + k, for k ∈ Q.

The proof given in that paper goes as follows.

Let f be the minimal polynomial of x over Q, and write y ∈ Q(x)ˣ as y = g(x). Transfer to a finite field containing both f and g. By a theorem of Kornblum-Artin, there exists a monic irreducible polynomial p of degree 2^n such that p ≡ g (mod f). Then p splits over Q, meaning g = ∏ k ∈ s, X + k and thus y = ∏ k ∈ s, x + k.

So then I look up the Kornblum-Artin theorem. And that states the following:

(Kornblum) Given f and g coprime polynomials over a finite field, there exists infinitely many monic irreducible polynomials p with p ≡ g (mod f). (Artin) And in fact, such a polynomial exists for every large enough degree.

I was able to find an exposition of this result in Michael Rosen's Number Theory in Function Fields (chapter 4). From what I can tell, the ideas are similar to the standard Dirichlet theorem. Except, you're now defining analogues of the zeta functions and L-series for ring 𝔽_q[X].

My question is: has there been any work on formalizing number theory over 𝔽_q[x]?
